title: Turn a competitor post into a customer question
hooks: That competitor post got a lot of views. Which customer question made it worth watching?
Before borrowing that hook, find the customer question underneath it.
A popular post can start your research. Your customer should shape the idea.
full_spoken_english: That competitor post got a lot of views. Which customer question made it worth watching? If you help market a small business, use the number to choose something to inspect. Keep the capture date beside it. Compare it with the same account's usual views. Then read what was said and look at what the viewer could actually see. Write three notes: the problem introduced, the useful answer, and the visual that made that answer clear. Now close the reference. Pick a question your own customers ask, and answer it with your own example. A high view count doesn't tell you which detail caused it. Treat your new idea as something to test, not a proven recipe. Before borrowing a hook, finish this sentence: our customer needs to understand blank. Build the post around that.
cta: Before borrowing a hook, finish this sentence: our customer needs to understand blank. Build the post around that.

fixture.input: Fictional reference: strong view count; opening names unclear appointment confirmations; workflow diagram shows a change branch.
fixture.designed_output: Customer question: How do I ask to change my booking? Original post idea: show the reply and reception handoff.
fixture.check: A new customer problem and original example, no copied line or causal claim.

audio_plan: Natural recorded voice; no imitation. Quiet room; optional subtle licensed music only after voice intelligibility check. No sound needed to understand proof panels.
caption_plan: Editable sentence captions, maximum two short lines; keep proof labels clear. Captions paraphrase nothing that changes a fact. Final platform safe-zone check after edit.
